title: Taskbase 2022 — "The world's #1 Feedback engine"
notes: First WordPress homepage: Elementor Pro on the Hello theme, with the "Supercharge your digital learning platform" hero typed out by typed.js and annotated with the product's own spellcheck cards. The "Why publishers and learning platforms trust in Taskbase" testimonial carousel was Slider Revolution 6.5.21. That is a paid ThemeForest plugin, so rs6.*, rbtools.*, revicons.*, its placeholder images and its revslider/svgcustom arrows were deleted before publication and the tags that loaded them are HTML comments now. The band is carried by the museum's own museum-slider.js and museum.css instead - a small vanilla slider, not the plugin. The four quotes, portraits, names and roles are this capture's own rs-slide content, verbatim, and the card sizing follows the module's own config (920px grid, 32px carousel space, 60px card padding); the motion, the arrows and the dots are ours. Elementor Pro's frontend, webpack runtime and element handlers went the same way, also for licensing; this capture never had the Pro widget chunks either, so the rest of the page renders as it did. A second museum-only CSS rule lays the ElementsKit partner-logo strip three across the way its own data-config (slidesPerView:3) had it, because its init script was never archived. Everything else is archive-original. Cookie banner, Google Tag Manager and HubSpot are stripped; the contact form posts nowhere. Dead hosts are repointed at a local not-archived/ path so the page never reaches the network.
